# Issue 2 Kato index repair: manuscript interface audit

Audit date: 7 November 2026. Scope: the missing index-set step in Issue 2, point 4. The current manuscript is `work/github-issue-review-20261107/quartic_v10-current.tex`, especially K4--K9 and lines 12680--12690. No manuscript or public issue was edited.

1. **Thin archimedean box, 16687–16695, GAU-004.** The required density is O(tau), while derivatives of the majorant may depend on tau. The source integrates in radial norm variables, whose difference has derivative bounded away from zero on the fixed positive norm range. This is an inline coarea/change-of-variables estimate. It does not assert uniform tau-dependent error constants.

2. **One-position medium sieve, 16763–16773, GAU-005.** This is a direct three-dimensional box-count input, not BL's five-dimensional theorem. For good ell and w nonzero, the k norm equations have disjoint zero sets. The distinguished norm-zero fibre has ell+(ell-1)chi elements, and the other fibres ell-chi. With the w=0 fibre included, the density is `(k+chi)/ell+O_k(ell^-2)`. The obstruction has a=0 and b²=-1, hence at most 2ell triples and density O(ell^-2). For any union of residues modulo squarefree m in a fixed smooth B-box, elementary lattice counting gives error bounded by `O(B²m+Bm²+m³)` after summing at most m³ classes, because each class contributes volume/m³ plus `O((B/m)²+B/m+1)`. In the actual range `m=ell[d,e] <= B^.03`, the Selberg double sum and ell sum remain much smaller than B^2.7. The same prime-harmonic and weighted-sieve calculation gives dimension k. Thus the short prose has a concrete supplier; treating it as an automatic application of BL would be wrong.

3. **Large-prime lattice basis, 16880–16913, GAU-007.** The basis comparable to Euclidean minima and the minima-product/determinant comparison are substantive geometric inputs. They are used to enclose the original B-box by coordinate sides O(B/lambda_i), volume O(B³/q²), and minimum side at least a constant B/T. They are also present in the BHB accepted proof, pp.16–18, extraction 692–832, examined by the prior tail review. The new graph retains them explicitly under BHB's proof method; the BHB lemma labels alone do not spell out this transition.

4. **Prime tail and divisor estimates, GAU-005/007/008.** Chebyshev's binomial argument is written in the medium proof and supplies the later sum over primes ell>L of ell^-2. The ordinary divisor bound and Rankin product bound supply the fixed-coordinate count. The divisor estimate follows by separating finitely many small primes in the prime factorization; `(e+1) <= C_epsilon p^(epsilon e)` gives tau(n) bounded by C_epsilon n^epsilon. The Rankin computation is displayed with its fixed exceptional prime set. These are retained as direct inputs; the sieve inventory's main named theorem does not replace them.

5. **Nilsequence geometry, GAU-015/022/026/030.** Nonzero horizontal characters push Haar measure to circle Haar measure; this and the rational-basis metric comparison give the short-arc obstruction. The rational conjugation step requires the lattice-index and metric estimates of GT Orbits Appendix A and the quantitative claim on p.547 of the published Mobius paper. The actual quotient is gamma_j^-1 G' gamma_j divided by its intersection with Gamma. These are not isometry claims about the old quotient.

6. **Ordinary majorant interval mean, GAU-037.** The constant-shift factor is either one or a single ordinary majorant. The source uses its mean on an interval of fixed relative length. The GT divisor-sum/linear-forms estimate on that interval supplies this input. The polynomial second moment concerns the remaining shifts with independent m,m', and weighted Cauchy–Schwarz supplies localization. This is not a pointwise logarithmic bound on the shrinking strip.

7. **Finite private-coordinate consumers, GAU-057/061/065/066/067/070.** Statements that eliminated inverses, powers or norm coordinates have no other consumers are computational assertions about the pinned straight-line program. They are not consequences of the displayed local algebra alone. The existing coefficient/elimination certificates and their independent review are the proposed suppliers. This pass records the dependence and preserves the old evidence scope; it did not replay those computations.

The consumer is `lem:v5-primitive-count`, fixed v13 lines 16650–16694, especially the BL call at 16665. The fixed manuscript hash is `9db71bbfcefb37db56eabcf40a5f9dd85de9ed58294635da3dbf6d4f5caa8fcd`. The relevant independent Gaussian contracts are GAU-003 and its downstream medium-prime consumers.

**DOCS-1 — template link context.** The original `../docs/...` links depended on the template file's location even though its text is consumed in a PR body. The final template uses the explicit public GitHub `blob/main/docs/research-review/README.md` and `blob/main/docs/research-review/PROTOCOL.md` targets. I checked the actual final text and identical public/private destination contents. I accept this repair. The URLs are navigation after incorporation, not immutable evidence or a claim that the documents were already on main. The exact reviewed contents remain bound by hashes above.

**SETUP-1 — reviewer report must be a Git blob.** A loose local report could not satisfy the stated evidence requirement. I directly obtained the predecessor `docs/research-review/SETUP-REVIEW.md` from both observed heads and verified its hash `b2d3b9e903bf7101bfd2e110db3b63bc2e253c93a07c4b1fa6ac8f7c1ac04e32`. That report was actual Git content and its changed path was explicit. The new opt02 report in the current table and this report must likewise be incorporated and then checked as actual Git blobs before final acceptance. I accept the repair method and predecessor incorporation, not an assertion that these newly revised reports are already in an unseen final tree. Final packets must bind the actual blobs, their genuine authors and the complete manifests; presence alone is not authenticated acceptance.

**SETUP-2 — final-head self-reference and report authorship.** I accept the proposed separation: freeze reviewer-authored content in Git, then obtain an external reviewer decision adopting those exact report bytes and the completed application/assembly targets after the final head exists. The report itself need not embed its own final-head hash. Every added report path must be included in changed-path coverage, and its actual author must remain recorded. Report authorship does not turn a reviewer into the author of the semantic policy they merely review; a substantive repair would be different and would reopen independence. No verdict or hash may be copied on a reviewer's behalf. This resolves the self-reference design issue without asserting that the not-yet-reviewed final external decision already exists.

**SETUP-3 — Windows text versus Git bytes.** I independently checked both predecessor working copies and both predecessor Git blobs. The prior working-copy `CONTRIBUTING.md` hash was `cd9b912f36b621b5fe3f7097837e89e527706382c9663907a26ac3869b518c76`, with exactly 32 CRLF pairs. Replacing exactly those pairs with LF gave the Git blob bytes exactly, whose hash was `4606405b80cf1dc4eaebf078424e820865fbf68d87c0843ee0a0c5f79a7227b7`. No other byte changes occurred. I read the corrected review's explicit acknowledgment and confirmed the preserved original report hash `35e90645b32785d1c73fbf51bc7ade36b2f1c2f8656411dd266eb573bc149eba`. I independently accept the correction authored by opt02. It corrects evidence binding and does not change the semantic guidance. The separately reviewed status edits now have the new bindings in the table, with independently checked normalization below. This finding must continue to identify opt02 as correction author and a distinct reviewer as its accepting reviewer.

Finding DOCS-1: the initial PR template used `../docs/research-review/README.md` and `../docs/research-review/PROTOCOL.md`. A template's text is inserted into a PR body; it is not rendered there as a file located in `.github`. Those relative targets therefore did not reliably identify the intended guide and protocol. This issue was reported during integration before this final semantic freeze.

## Finite callers and the preserved defect

The related-use record correctly preserves the large-offset issue, equal-side restriction, false rational-Taylor deletion and left/right period issue. The new proof supplies the first and the needed alternative routes for the latter issues within this bounded scope. In particular it does not establish D.5's false Taylor conclusion. MF-F04 and later E11/E13 applications remain with the other reviewer. No blanket no-import classification or whole-GI acceptance is issued.

The exact consumer is the periodicity clause of DF-D4, propagated through the closure lemma and minimal-subgroup descent and then consumed by the one-variable D6 factorization argument. The result is a standard positive period valid for all internal integers. This local review accepts that clause under the proof's fixed-group, fixed-degree and common-coordinate-denominator premises. It does not independently reaccept every construction of the overgroup, the rest of DF-D4, DF-F1, the Gaussian Sections 9–11 argument, or any multivariable equidistribution theorem.

I read the whole local argument and checked the corresponding final GTZ Sections 9–11 text, including the horizontal convention in Definition 9.6 and the actual Theorem 11.1/Corollary 11.4 consumers. In the horizontal formula at i=1 use the source convention G_(1,2)=G_(2,0). Fixed positive-weight rational lattice generators lift each horizontal frequency to the universal torus. The integer change of letters realizes the frequency map exactly. The bad-set diagonal argument gives a fixed relation on a dense set when independence fails. The core-only case drops one core. A relation in the first three linear blocks fixes two parameters and drops one linear coordinate. If any independent block appears, a symmetry places its nonzero coefficient in position four, the Freiman identity eliminates the omitted fourth linear block, and DF-F1 recovers the fourth function on a dense set. Choosing roots and retaining the finite carries gives the required integer representation with one fewer independent coordinate. Fixed-box refinement restores exact Freiman behavior. Previous sparse bad sets remain sparse under dense restriction.

I also checked the final Milne 1986 source at printed 114–115 and 122, using the existing pinned scan, and its public errata note. Those statements are consistent with the image/isogeny interpretation and identify the separate Poincare premise. The imperfect-field qualification to the proof of Proposition 12.1 does not affect Q. This review does not import or reapprove my earlier B11 endomorphism-lattice correction.
